factCheckIssues.problem: The draft defines a deposit as a loan 'repayable on demand or on agreed terms'. That is not the statutory definition, which turns on the interest or premium element.

factCheckIssues.fix: Rewrote the definition to follow the statute. Also added the 'deposit' definition to the provisions[2] summary.

factCheckIssues.problem: The draft presented internet 'targeting' as statutory text. It is the MA's policy, set out in a guideline under s.92(6), and applies to offshore internet material.

factCheckIssues.fix: Attributed the targeting test to the s.92(6) guideline (May 2002) and confined it to offshore internet material. Raised confidence to high.

factCheckIssues.problem: Group 2 exposures attract a 1250% risk weight
factCheckIssues.evidence: Capital Rules s.385(1): 1,250% risk weight applies to Group 2b exposures in the banking book, on the greater of aggregate long and short positions. Group 2a uses modified market-risk approaches (ss.381-383) and Group 2a derivatives have a 32% SA-CCR supervisory factor.

factCheckIssues.problem: Group 2 limit (1% generally, never above 2% of Tier 1) implemented by L.N. 152 (Exposure Limits)
factCheckIssues.evidence: Capital Rules s.387 (all AIs calculate the group 2 cryptoasset exposure ratio, Formula 32E) and s.388 (G-SIBs and D-SIBs only: must not exceed 1%; between 1% and 2% notify MA, add-on, rectify; above 2% full Group 2b-equivalent add-on). Banking (Exposure Limits) Rules as amended by L.N. 152 add Division 5A valuation of cryptoasset-related exposures for large-exposure counterparty limits; no 1%/2% Group 2 limit found there.

factCheckIssues.problem: Unclassified crypto is capitalised close to full deduction
